title: The 8 Show
hook: How does The 8 Show end? The Fibonacci floors, the riot, and Floor 1's fatal tightrope act in the Season 1 finale, explained.

sections.heading: A game built on time and inequality
sections.body: Eight participants are locked inside a building where they earn money based purely on how much time elapses. Each floor pays out on a Fibonacci sequence, so the higher floors accumulate vastly more than the lower ones, and they enjoy far better accommodations too. At first the players cooperate to stretch the game time and maximise everyone's earnings. The arrangement only holds until they grasp how brutally unequal the payouts are, at which point the shared interest that kept them civil starts to curdle into resentment between the levels.

sections.heading: Violence becomes the currency
sections.body: The turning point arrives when Floor 7 realises that time, and therefore money, is added because the fights are entertaining to whoever is watching them. Suffering is the product. Once that is understood the game mutates into a spectacle, and the players begin staging brutal contests involving tasers and baseball bats to keep the clock and the cash running. A power struggle hardens between the upper floors, six, seven, eight and four, and the lower floors, one, two, three and five, as the building splits into rulers and ruled feeding an unseen audience.

sections.heading: Floor 1's tightrope and the fire
sections.body: The endgame belongs to Floor 1, a circus performer who entered the show to afford treatment for his daughter's rare disease. In the finale he holds the other players captive and performs a tightrope act above them. Bouncing higher and higher, he manages to grab a projector mounted in the ceiling, but it comes loose under his weight. He plummets down into flames that have engulfed the space, and dies from the burns. His desperate, theatrical sacrifice is what finally brings the whole game crashing to its end.

sections.heading: Who walks out, and the story retold
sections.body: With Floor 1 dead and the game over, the survivors are the players from Floors 2, 3, 4 and 5. The aftermath ties off the human cost. Floor 7 gives Floor 1's wife enough money to live on for the rest of her life, honouring the man whose death ended things. Floor 8 is arrested for destroying an art gallery. In the final turn, Floor 7 writes a screenplay about the ordeal titled The 8 Show, folding the players' suffering back into the very kind of entertainment that drove the whole nightmare.

final_image: Floor 7 turns the ordeal into a screenplay titled The 8 Show, the survivors' suffering recycled into the same spectacle that fed the audience who profited from their pain.

lingering_questions.a: During his tightrope act he bounces high enough to grab a ceiling projector, but it comes loose and he falls into the flames below, dying from the burns. His death brings the game to an end.
The players from Floors 2, 3, 4 and 5 survive. Floor 7 later gives Floor 1's wife enough money for life, while Floor 8 is arrested for destroying an art gallery.
